title.source: The Kaḍambāwa Men and the Mouse-deer

markdown_file: Asia/Sri Lanka (Sinhalese people)/042 - The Kaḍambāwa Men and the Mouse-deer.md

segments.source: The Kaḍambāwa men having appointed a wedding-[day], and having caught a great many Mouse-deer [for eating at it], tied clappers on their necks like those on goats, and having made an enclosure put them in it, and came away.
The Mouse-deer escaped into the jungle.
Having gone to it on the wedding-day, when they looked there was not one Mouse-deer left.
The Mouse-deer that we reared have all gone,” came back to the village, much astonished.
